chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ibn Sinan, from Salih ibn Uqba, from Abdullah ibn Muhammad al-Ju'fi, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:

The most rightful of Allah's creatures to submit to what Allah has decreed is the one who knows Allah, and the one who is satisfied with the Decree; the Decree comes upon him, and Allah magnifies his reward. And the one who is displeased with the Decree, the Decree passes over him, and Allah nullifies his reward.
ai.seo_question: What is the difference between those who are satisfied with God's decree and those who are displeased with it?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi links intellectual recognition of Allah (ma'rifah) with emotional acceptance (rida), establishing that true knowledge manifests in contentment with divine decree. It highlights the eschatological consequence of this state: those who accept Allah's will with gratitude see their spiritual reward elevated, whereas those who resent it incur the loss of their deeds. This reflects the Shia emphasis on the unity of gnosis and volition in achieving nearness to God.
